prompt: Which row correctly classifies the four quantities?
options: distance: scalar; displacement: scalar; speed: vector; velocity: vector
distance: scalar; displacement: vector; speed: scalar; velocity: vector
distance: vector; displacement: scalar; speed: vector; velocity: scalar
distance: vector; displacement: vector; speed: scalar; velocity: scalar

answer.explanation: B. Distance and speed are scalars. Displacement and velocity are vectors.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 classifies displacement as scalar and speed as vector, reversing both.
Option 2 correctly classifies distance and speed as scalars, and displacement and velocity as vectors.
Option 3 classifies distance as vector and velocity as scalar, which is incorrect.
Option 4 classifies distance as vector and speed as scalar, incorrectly reversing distance.
hints: Ask whether direction is needed to describe each quantity completely.
Distance and speed describe magnitude only. Displacement and velocity also require direction.
solution: B. Distance and speed are scalars. Displacement and velocity are vectors.
teacher_walkthrough: Start with distance. A distance such as 12 m is complete without a direction, so distance is a scalar.
Speed is also complete with magnitude and unit only, so speed is a scalar.
Displacement describes a change in position in a specified direction, so it is a vector.
Velocity is the rate of change of displacement. It also has direction, so it is a vector. Therefore B is correct.
